scope_records.conclusion: Definitions duplicate respectively A5 and C2×A5; printed figure names are transposed.

Halving any regular lattice polytope of rank n≥3 produces a C-group.
Actual halving coset incidence is flag-transitive.
Halving gives a regular hypertope with changed group as full type-preserving group.
Index is at most2, exactly2 iff the appropriate vertex/facet graph is bipartite; duplicate adjacent labels and halve an even endpoint order.
Exact halving group E_m⋊Aut(K) in the source dual convention, order2^(m−1)|Aut(K)| with m the facet count.

scope_records.exact_target: For an ordinary map, the chamber-defined walk is its conventional Petrie walk.

scope_records.exact_target: The geometrically defined Petrial is residually connected.
scope_records.historical_adapter: Walk connectivity of new face residues and path replacements in old vertex/edge residues; connected old vertex-edge truncation derived directly.

scope_records.exact_target: Unconditional embedding of original type-preserving automorphism group in that of its Petrial.
scope_records.remaining_obligation: No claim about historical priority of this explicit boundary.
scope_records.historical_adapter: Natural homomorphism exists with kernel contained in <a>; K_(2,2,2) gives original group C2^3 and Petrial group C2^2.

scope_records.exact_target: For a thin Petrial, applying the Petrial twice recovers the original geometry.
scope_records.historical_adapter: After the principal obstruction, vertex-edge interchange reduces to [a,c]=1; the new marking is (a,b,ca), the second shift cb, and old face shadows are proved distinct.

scope_records.exact_target: The original and thin-Petrial automorphism groups agree via their retained-object action.
scope_records.historical_adapter: Face-residue transitivity gives regularity of the induced action; its panel action forces a outside the kernel and hence faithfulness.
K_(2,2,2) has linear diagram but its Petrial has one face and is nonthin. Earlier atlas examples are not reproduced.
C2 times S3 has chamber step order6 but only3 vertices and3 edges in its Petrie set; uniform proofs do not require the equality.
